scope: Isolated Chrome controls for reconstructing independent numeric arrays from a browser-private file; not a ScanForge restore or production change.
method: Separate guarded headless Chrome runs generated 16777216 Float64 values, including negative zero, and checked every reconstructed value. The baseline copied a resident buffer into a pre-sized ordinary array. The staged case wrote the buffer to an origin-private file in 2 MiB pieces, detached the original buffer, then reconstructed the same array from 2 MiB file slices. A second staged variant detached each read buffer immediately after copying. A third recorded aggregate Chrome process groups at each stage.

results.processObservation: In the instrumented run, the browser process private-byte sample rose from 39284736 at baseline to 173117440 after staging and source detachment. This is process accounting, not an identified allocation or proof of causation.

limitations: These single synthetic controls do not reproduce a full project restore or establish that all file-backed staging designs are infeasible.
Process sampling adds work and separate-run memory varies. The browser process observation does not identify the allocation.
No prototype is integrated; restore ownership, resource, native-comparison and M2 closure gates remain open.
